body:
# Independent audit: relative-mesh recovery through compact intrinsic lifts



One notation clarification was sent to the author: the lifted point in Section 3 is `(z,E_i x,G(z))`, with x in its component's m-block, rather than the unembedded tuple `(z,x,G(z))`. This does not change the argument or constants.

## 1. Uniform fine/coarse discrepancy

Every original coarse fiber lies in the fixed ball R B_m and hence in the coordinate cube [-R,R]^m. For each closed ambient halfspace H, its slice in a coarse fiber is a compact convex set, possibly lower-dimensional or empty. The previously audited sampling estimate therefore gives the same bound

    E_l=2r delta_l(2R+2delta_l)^(m-1)

for all such slices, including fibers of zero full m-volume. Summing over J=|P| bounds both the halfspace error and the total-mass error by J E_l. No fine mass on a zero-coarse-volume fiber is discarded.

Since M_l<=J kappa_m R^m, the hypothesis delta_l/M_l->0 implies delta_l->0 and J E_l/M_l->0. The fine total is eventually positive, and the normalized halfspace error is at most

    2J E_l/(M_l-J E_l).

This normalization remains valid when M_l tends to zero. It is uniform halfspace discrepancy, not total variation between the singular sampled measure and coarse Lebesgue measure. All closed supporting boundaries are included.

## 2. Retained support, conditional center, and quantifiers

Starting with an arbitrary subsequence realizing the liminf and then extracting convergent normalized coarse weights is sufficient. The positive limiting support is finite, nonempty, and lattice-convex. Compatibility gives a target volume at least lambda^m times any positive source volume in an anchored representation. Retaining its full fibers yields their exact original fiber identities in their convex hull. Their total M_(l,+) satisfies M_(l,+)/M_l->1.

The saturated base-rank reduction leaves the original continuous coordinates unchanged. The full-shape lift theorem then gives positive m-dimensional residual limits and a full ambient convex lift at integer rank k'<=k, continuous dimension

    m<=D<=B(k',m)<=B(k,m),
    B(k,m)=(m+1)2^k-k-1.

The input OC theorem is explicitly required for this intrinsic lower-dimensional intersection in continuous ambient dimension D. The proof uses its Gamma_D bound, not an unproved Gamma_m strengthening. When k=0 the single fiber is full m-dimensional and ordinary Grünbaum is the only input.

The compact lift's exact component isolation supplies depth continuity when moving a point inside its own residual m-plane. A limit center can therefore be perturbed into the relative interior with an arbitrarily small fixed depth loss epsilon. A fixed interior residual point x has a ball x+rho B_m inside every sufficiently late residual fiber. The radius rho can depend on the extracted limit and epsilon; the argument never needs it uniform over all original sequences or as epsilon tends to zero.

Residual total variation controls all cap masses at this same point. The global affine pullback gives its retained coarse depth, and multiplication by M_(l,+)/M_l gives its full coarse depth. This establishes the pre-rounding lower bound without any convergence assumption on the affine pullback maps or their oblique coefficients.

## 3. The quantitative source ball

For the selected component let A_l=T_(l,i)^(-1). Its absolute determinant is M_(l,+). The mapped residual ball gives

    w_l+rho A_l B_m subset K_(l,z) subset R B_m.

Taking diameters of opposite points of this ellipsoid yields

    sigma_max(A_l)<=R/rho.

The product of the m singular values is M_(l,+), so

    sigma_min(A_l)>=M_(l,+)(rho/R)^(m-1).

Consequently the actual original coarse fiber contains

    w_l+[rho^m/R^(m-1)] M_(l,+) B_m.

The determinant here is the m-dimensional fiber Jacobian of the source map. It is not the total-dimensional Jacobian of the enlarged lift. The proof remains valid at m=1: the product of the other singular values is the empty product one.

All offsets and component-constant terms cancel from the diameter estimate. No boundedness of those offsets is required; boundedness of the original fiber itself is exactly the needed hypothesis.

## 4. Deterministic feasible rounding

The lattice cells tile almost everywhere and are contained in their centered coordinate cubes. The union of the corresponding CLOSED cubes is locally finite and closed, with open null complement, so it covers every point of R^r. This justifies deterministic rounding even at an omitted fundamental-cell boundary.

Round only the u coordinates of w_l to a lattice point within Euclidean distance sqrt(r) delta_l. The other s coordinates and the coarse integer base are unchanged. Since

    delta_l/M_l->0,   M_(l,+)/M_l->1,

this displacement is eventually smaller than the source-ball radius above. The rounded point is in the actual original fine mixed set. The proof never applies T_(l,i) to the fine lattice.

For every coarse halfspace with nonzero m-dimensional continuous normal, normalization of that part gives a threshold change at most the rounding distance in each coarse fiber. The maximal section area in R B_m is at most kappa_(m-1)R^(m-1). Hence the normalized coarse depth loss is at most

    J kappa_(m-1)R^(m-1)sqrt(r) delta_l/M_l=o(1).

Pure coarse-base normals are unchanged. This estimate allows arbitrarily large coarse integer coefficients and arbitrary mixing of the u and x coordinates. Zero-full-volume coarse fibers do not contribute to this coarse slab estimate, while their fine mass was already included in the separate sampling error.

At the same feasible rounded point the normalized halfspace discrepancy transfers the coarse bound to fine depth. Thus every extracted liminf subsequence has lower limit at least

    2^(-k')Gamma_D-epsilon >=2^(-k)Gamma_(B(k,m))-epsilon.

Letting epsilon tend to zero after this argument proves the stated global liminf bound. Dependence of rho on epsilon and the extracted subsequence causes no quantifier gap.

## 5. Constants and intrinsic boundary cases

For m>=1, B(k,m)>=1. Therefore Gamma_(B(k,m))>1/e>1/4. If s>=1, then Gamma_s<=1/2 and r>=1, so

    2^(-k)Gamma_(B(k,m))
      >2^(-k)/4>=2^(-k-r)Gamma_s.

The strict gap converts the liminf statement to an eventual single-point target bound. For s=0 and r>=2 the same comparison works with Gamma_0=1. The excluded case s=0,r=1 does not follow from this comparison; the note correctly refers to the separate pure-integer theorem instead.

The common lattice covolume factor cancels from normalized fine depth. Eventual positivity of the sampled s-volume implies that the fine source has Hausdorff dimension exactly s; when s=0 it is a nonempty finite counting source. Thus the comparison is with the intended intrinsic fine measure, not a measure that has silently changed dimension.

No further corrections or missing estimates were found. The unresolved applicability issue is exactly the one stated in the source: delta_l/M_l need not tend to zero in a general normalized sequence.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
